definitions: A pathological hardening of tissue, especially from overgrowth of fibrous tissue or increase in interstitial tissue.

A chronic progressive disease of the central nervous system marked by the demyelination of nerve fibres, with the formation of plaques, or hardened areas, in the brain and spinal cord, resulting in the impairment of motor, sensory, and autonomic functions.
examples: The patient was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis.
Arterial sclerosis can lead to serious health problems.
The sclerosis of the liver was advanced.
